about: Stages and timing for the product-opportunity playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: find
stages.do: Sort the account's products into opportunity groups, add the top ones as findings, and ask the user which product to take forward.

stages.name: report
stages.do: Report the chosen product everywhere: performance against its peers, positions, rules and stock. Decide whether ranking or the listing is the problem.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found no product worth acting on.

stages.name: listing
stages.do: Suggest a better title, description, attributes and alt text for the product, for the feed team to import. Skip it when the listing is sound.

skip_when.reason: the product report found nothing to change.

stages.name: test
stages.do: A/B test boosting (or burying) the product on its main query or category, and start it after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the listing, not ranking, is the problem; or there's nothing to change.

stages.name: read-out
stages.do: Read the test's result. Don't stop early on a good-looking day.

stages.name: close
stages.do: End the test keeping the winner (or today's ranking), check every rule, then archive it, each step after its own yes.

stages.name: confirm
stages.do: Check the shipped boost or bury holds at full traffic, with the rule and its live date from the hand-off file.

skip_when.reason: nothing changed for shoppers, so there is nothing to confirm.

notes.min_test_days: Days after the test stage finishes (the test started) before the read-out stage is due. discovery-experiment-setup recommends at least 14 days in whole weeks; use the end date agreed at setup when it's later.
notes.measure_after_days: Days after the close stage finishes (the winner went to full traffic) before the confirm stage is due. change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days of data after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes, or was skipped).
